newsitem.title: UK: ZCCM sees copper shipments normal by end-November.
newsitem.headline: ZCCM sees copper shipments normal by end-November.

text.p: Delays to Zambian copper shipments due to rail difficulties are being ironed out at present and conditions should be back to normal by the end of November, Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines Ltd (ZCCM) sources in London said.
ZCCM officials met last week with the management of the railway company, who provided them with assurances of extra locomotives and reduced rail congestion, the sources said.
"We expect and hope that we will get back to normal by the end of November," one source said.
Tazara railway management also said they would triple the number of locomotives and have adequate fuel supplies, he said.
ZCCM transports its copper from Zambia via the Tazara railway through the port of Dar-es-Salaam, but has experienced recent difficulties due to various logistical problems.
These resulted in transit times for copper stretching from the usual 12 days to 21 days recently.
The sources declined to say what tonnage of copper had been delayed, but said ZCCM had stepped up the volume of traffic through the alternative ports of Beira, Durban and East London.
Because of this the delays were not serious enough to justify any thoughts of force majeure, they said.
